messages:
micah: FYI trying to provision a new gpu-nodepool in us-west3 with 4 x A10G nodes and the create failed with "no available IPs in subnet". need ideas for short-term mitigation and long-term fix.

sara: ouch. which subnet / CIDR? sounds like secondary-range shortage for pod IPs?

micah: subnet is projects/redwood-vpc/regions/us-west3/subnetworks/gpu-pool-subnet (10.2.8.0/24) — we already have other clusters sharing the secondary range for pods. cloud console shows secondary-range used up.

ashwin: can we move the pool to a different subnet with spare /22? otherwise options: increase secondary range, split nodepool across 2 subnets, or reduce maxPodsPerNode to pack fewer pod IPs per node.

lisa: reducing maxPods helps but impacts kube-scheduler density and may raise latency for per-GPU small jobs. also won't help if nodes need hostIPs for pods that require hostNetwork.

micah: short term I tried creating a nodepool with smaller instance type (a2-highgpu-1g) to fit within current quota but the service team prefers A10G for throughput.

ashwin: there's also an ENI/internal IP quota (GCP: alias IPs) we should check — sometimes the cloud returns IP shortage even with CIDR because of per-region internal IP quota.

micah: checked quotas: "network/addresses" and "subnetworks secondary IP ranges" look fine, but the VPC's secondary-pool for pods is at 100% usage.

infra-bot: [alert] quota-usage: gpu-pool-subnet secondary-range at 100% (10.2.8.0/24). This is blocking new node allocations.

daniela: short-term workaround: create a temporary per-cluster secondary range and attach it to the subnet, then create the nodepool in that cluster. ops will need to request a bigger CIDR from cloud infra.

sara: we could also create the nodepool in us-west3-a only (single AZ) and use a custom secondary range that we dole out to that cluster, but that reduces AZ redundancy. tradeoffs?

lisa: another idea: use our Dedicated burst pool in us-west2 and route traffic via service mesh (latency trade-off). cheaper to spin there than to rework subnets fast.

ashwin: longer term: recommend adopting per-cluster/namespace secondary ranges with automated CIDR management (see gist: https://go.example.com/cidr-manager). avoid shared global secondary range for pods.

micah: action items I can take now: 1) open cloud support ticket to expand secondary range for gpu-pool-subnet, 2) spin up a temporary secondary-range attached to the subnet and create a short-lived nodepool using smaller SKU, 3) evaluate moving heavy traffic to us-west2 burst pool. anyone want to own the support ticket?

sara: I can own the quota ticket. will CC infra-sd and include the error logs.

micah: thanks. rough gcloud commands I used earlier: ```
# attempt - fails due to alias IP exhaustion
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-a10g-pool --cluster=prod-infer --zone=us-west3-a --machine-type=a10g-1 --num-nodes=4 --max-pods-per-node=30
```

micah: attempt to add secondary range (blocked by policy): ```
gcloud compute networks subnets expand --region=us-west3 --subnet=gpu-pool-subnet --add-secondary-range=pods-2=10.2.16.0/20
```

ashwin: note: some org policies prevent expanding subnets programmatically, you'll need network-admin to approve. also check VPC peering configs if you attach new ranges.

daniela: cost note: switching to smaller GPU SKUs increases per-token latency and may require doubling replicas. estimate cost delta ~+35% for same throughput if moving from A10G to A2; include in ticket as consequence.

lisa: cluster-autoscaler config reminder: if we create a mixed nodepool fallback make sure to set label gpu-tier and taint nvgpu=true:NoSchedule so we don't schedule non-GPU workloads there. also set scaleDownUtilizationThreshold to 0.1 for burst pools.

micah: good call. proto nodepool spec I was experimenting with: ```
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: ContainerNodePool
metadata:
  name: gpu-burst-temp
spec:
  initialNodeCount: 2
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 0
    maxNodeCount: 8
  nodeConfig:
    machineType: a2-highgpu-1g
    taints:
    - key: nvgpu
      value: true
      effect: NO_SCHEDULE
    labels:
      pool: gpu-burst
```

sara: ok I'll include the autoscaling fallback plan in the ticket so support has context.

ashwin: after ticket is filed, let's run an IP usage audit across all clusters to find reclaimable ranges. I have a script that lists cluster secondary ranges: ```
./scripts/list-allocated-secondary-ranges.sh --project redwood-vpc
```

micah: pinging @network-admins and @platform-leads for permission to expand/attach secondary ranges.

infra-bot: [deploy] created temp gpu-burst namespace in staging for testing (job id: deploy-8842).

daniela: follow-up: we should update our provisioning runbook to include a subnet-capacity check before issuing nodepool create in any region. I can draft changes.

micah: perfect — I'll hold off on nodepool creation until we get a support response or spin up temp burst in us-west2. thanks all :thumbsup:
